Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2) demonstrates bilateral pulmonary nodules and prominent hilar lymphadenopathy, which are classic radiographic features of sarcoidosis. The accompanying CT scan (Figure 1a) confirms bilateral hilar adenopathy and parenchymal nodules, consistent with the "sarcoid galaxy sign" described in option B, whereas options like heart failure or metastatic disease do not typically present with this specific combination of symmetric hilar enlargement and nodularity.
